coverage: Week of October 4-10, 2026 (YouVersion release dated October 6, 2026)

feature.title: Anxiety, hope and healing: what people searched for in the Bible App this year
feature.why: This is a Bible app's own yearly data on what people bring to Scripture. 'Anxiety', 'hope' and 'healing' were top searches and 'Psalm 91' was the most-searched term. Daily readers rose more than 13% to 18.5 million. The app offers 3,800 Bible versions in 2,400 languages, and the November 30-Day Bible Challenge adds friend progress tracking. The story sits squarely on technology helping people draw near to Christ through His Word, it is primary-sourced and dated inside the window, and YouVersion is not in topic memory. Writer note: the release includes regional rankings, regional hubs and city activations. Omit all of that under the no-geography rule and use only the worldwide figures and search themes.

alsoEncouraging.title: Ascension releases a dyslexia-friendly Catholic Bible set in the research-tested Grace typeface
Gloo AI Hackathon's Best of Bible award goes to Envoy Mission, an offline, private Bible app shared through AI conversations with seekers

wisdomConcern: Search data measures need, not transformation. A verse search or a reading streak is not the same as discipleship within a church, and growing AI-generated Scripture media (such as Pray.com's new sermon-to-video studio) risks turning the Word into content to consume. Also note that the app holds sensitive data on what people search in their struggles.
